title: CedarDB wants one database to handle both transactions and analytics, as AI agents raise the stakes
slides: CedarDB handles transactions and analytics together. But can it survive AI agents?
AI agents query databases differently, mixing reads and writes unpredictably.
CedarDB's secret is a unified engine that treats both workloads equally.
You can run analytics on live transactional data without copying it.
Test your next analytics query directly on production — carefully.
thread_text:
1. AI Agents vs. CedarDB

CedarDB claims to handle transactions and analytics in one engine. But AI agents don't query like humans — they mix reads and writes unpredictably. Can it keep up?

2. The Real Problem

AI agents don't follow the usual read-then-write pattern. They jump between selecting and inserting without warning, breaking the assumptions databases were built on.

3. One Engine, Two Workloads

CedarDB's unified engine treats transactional and analytical queries the same. No separate systems, no copying data between them. That's how it survives the chaos.

4. Live Data, No Copies

You can run analytics directly on live transactional data. No ETL, no stale snapshots. Agents get real-time answers without moving a byte.

5. Try It, Carefully

Take your next analytics query and run it on production — just watch the load. Does your database handle mixed workloads without falling over? Test it this week.

instagram.caption:
AI agents don't read then write. They jump between selecting and inserting with no warning, breaking how databases were built.

CedarDB runs transactions and analytics in one engine instead of two separate systems. No copying data, no ETL, no stale snapshots. 🧠

That means analytics can run directly on live transactional data, even while agents query the same tables. ⚡

If your pipeline still moves data between systems before analyzing it, this architecture is worth a look before your agents get heavier. 🛠️

Would you dare run your next analytics query on production — or does your database fall over first? 👀
